findings.title: Exit-code contract changed for recreate and feature-disabled reuses old code
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED is assigned 4. The update-compatibility check command is documented as scriptable and users are told to rely on its exit codes. Any existing automation that interpreted exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will now interpret it as 'rolling-updates feature disabled'. If the command has already been consumed, this is a breaking contract change.

findings.title: Documented exit codes are not asserted in CLI tests
findings.body: The PR introduces exit code 4 for a disabled feature and changes the recreate exit code to 3, and the documentation tells users to rely on these exit codes. However the distribution tests only assert messages: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4, testCompatible does not assert the check command exits 0, and testWrongVersions does not assert exit code 3. Add exit-code assertions to protect the scripted contract.

findings.title: Feature list is overwritten with an immutable list
findings.body: createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())) after only checking whether FeatureSpec is null. If a FeatureSpec already contains enabled features, they are silently replaced, and the stored list is immutable. Later test code or framework code that appends features will throw UnsupportedOperationException. Preserve existing entries and use a mutable list when adding rolling-updates.
